identity.title: Harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur, late-peaking, radiating to carotids, with soft/absent A2

technique.how: With the patient supine or sitting forward in end-expiration, listen with the diaphragm at the right 2nd intercostal space and along the left sternal border. Note the timing of peak intensity (early vs mid/late systole), radiation to the right carotid/clavicle, and whether A2 is soft or inaudible.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet room; palpate carotid simultaneously to time systole; examiner able to distinguish S1/S2.

interpretation.positive_finding: Late-peaking ejection murmur with soft/absent A2 and carotid radiation strongly favours moderate-or-greater aortic stenosis (pooled LR ~11 for diminished S2).
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of a murmur radiating to the neck makes moderate-or-greater AS unlikely (pooled LR- 0.11); an early-peaking murmur points away from severe AS.
interpretation.pitfalls: Loudness does not track severity; low-flow severe AS may give a soft murmur. Aortic sclerosis and HCM produce similar ejection murmurs, and murmur detection itself has only fair interobserver agreement.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: obtain echocardiography and treat exertional syncope/angina as possible severe AS. Negative (no neck radiation): AS becomes an unlikely cause and workup shifts elsewhere.

estimates.population: Adults with systolic murmur or suspected AS undergoing echocardiography/catheterization (7 observational studies, 1984-1998)
estimates.reference_standard: Echocardiography or left heart catheterization; AS of at least moderate severity
estimates.quote: Auscultating a diminished second heart sound (likelihood ratio [LR] = 10.87, 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.94-30.12
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; Table 2 (diminished S2 row: sensitivity 0.59 [0.44-0.72], specificity 0.95 [0.85-0.98], LR- 0.44 [0.31-0.61])

estimates.population: Adults with systolic murmur or suspected AS undergoing echocardiography/catheterization (7 observational studies, 1984-1998)
estimates.reference_standard: Echocardiography or left heart catheterization; AS of at least moderate severity
estimates.quote: The absence of a systolic murmur radiating to the neck (LR = 0.11, 95% CI, 0.06-0.23, P < 0.05)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; Table 2 (systolic murmur radiating to the neck row: sensitivity 0.93 [0.81-0.97], specificity 0.66 [0.41-0.84], LR+ 2.69 [1.48-4.89])

estimates.population: Narrative aggregate of 4 small studies of patients with systolic murmurs (not bivariate meta-analysed)
estimates.reference_standard: Echocardiography or left heart catheterization; AS of at least moderate severity
estimates.quote: Data from a small sample from 4 studies revealed modest positive predictive value when this sign is present (LR of 3.7)
estimates.location: Discussion, paragraph on murmur characteristics (same paragraph: 'negative predictive value of its absence (LR = 0.2)')

sources.citation: Shellenberger RA, Crass S, Jevicks J, Badhwar A, Albright J, Kumar A. Bedside Physical Examination for the Diagnosis of Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. CJC Open. 2023;5(5):373-379.
Etchells E, Bell C, Robb K. Does this patient have an abnormal systolic murmur? JAMA. 1997;277(7):564-571.
Etchells E, Glenns V, Shadowitz S, Bell C, Siu S. A bedside clinical prediction rule for detecting moderate or severe aortic stenosis. J Gen Intern Med. 1998;13(10):699-704.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use the murmur alone to exclude AS in low-output states or when the exam is limited by obesity/COPD; image if the clinical picture (exertional syncope, angina, HF) suggests AS.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Suspected severe AS with syncope, angina or heart failure needs urgent echocardiography and cardiology input; avoid aggressive vasodilators or diuresis until severity is known.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Detection of systolic murmurs has only fair reliability (kappa 0.30-0.48, Etchells 1997); no reliability data for murmur peak timing were found.

extraction_notes: Pooled estimates for diminished S2 and neck radiation taken from CJC Open 2023 meta-analysis (PMC full text, Table 2). Late-peaking murmur was not meta-analysed (only 2 studies pooled-eligible); the LR 3.7 / 0.2 values are a narrative aggregate reported in the Discussion with no CIs, so evidence_level 'pooled' is approximate. Etchells 1997 RCE reports only LR ranges (mid-to-late peak LR+ 8.0-101; decreased S2 LR+ 3.1-50; absent right-carotid radiation LR- 0.05-0.10) and its tables were not viewable, so no point estimate was entered from it. Etchells 1998 cited for the combined prediction rule (3-4 associated findings LR 40, 95% CI 6.6-240; absent right-clavicle murmur LR 0.10) rather than as an individual-sign estimate.
